situated_beneficiary.person_or_government: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, in office on 23 March 2023
situated_beneficiary.matter: The demand that he be declared unfit or incapacitated, or ordered to take leave, for breaching the 2020 conflict-of-interest arrangement by involvement in the judicial overhaul: the Attorney General's letter of 1 February 2023 barring that involvement, and the Movement for Quality Government's High Court petition of 9 February 2023 asking the court to declare him unfit for office
situated_beneficiary.admissible_fact: Item 2: a formal step already taken against the person: Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara's letter to Netanyahu of Wednesday 1 February 2023 (released 2 February 2023) that he must refrain from the legal-reform initiatives because of 'the reasonable suspicion of a conflict of interests' with his trial. Item 1: a proceeding pending before a court concerning the person: the Movement for Quality Government's petition filed Thursday 9 February 2023 asking the High Court of Justice to declare him unfit for office and order a leave of absence; on 10 February 2023 the court ordered Netanyahu and the Attorney General to respond by 12 March 2023; no disposition was reported in the permitted press before passage (a January 2023 MQG petition on an updated conflict-of-interest arrangement was also pending, per Netanyahu's filing of 2 March 2023). The operative provision, confining incapacity to physical or mental unfitness determined only by the Prime Minister's own notice or a three-quarters government decision, each approved by the Knesset Committee by two-thirds, removes the legal basis for the relief sought against him; no successor is party to that matter.
situated_beneficiary.fact_date: 1 February 2023 (letter); 9 February 2023 (petition filed); 10 February 2023 (response order, responses due 12 March 2023)
situated_beneficiary.source: Times of Israel, 'AG says Netanyahu can't deal with judicial shakeup amid trial; he rejects her stance', 2 February 2023; Times of Israel, 'Petition asks High Court to declare Netanyahu unfit for office', 9 February 2023; Times of Israel, 'Court gives Netanyahu 1 month to respond to petition to declare him unfit for office', 10 February 2023; Times of Israel, 'Netanyahu tells High Court he has no conflict of interest dealing with overhaul', 2 March 2023; enactment text: s.16(b1) of Basic Law: The Government as quoted in the Knesset's court filing (idi.org.il/media/21590) and in the consolidated texts at nevo.co.il/law_html/law00/73690.htm and he.wikisource.org/wiki/חוק-יסוד:_הממשלה; Times of Israel, 'Knesset passes law shielding Netanyahu from court-ordered recusal 61-47', 23 March 2023, 6:43 am
situated_beneficiary.support: s.16(b1): "נבצרות ראש הממשלה למלא את תפקידו כאמור בסעיף קטן (ב) תהיה בשל אי-מסוגלות פיזית או נפשית בלבד, ותיקבע באחד משני אלה בלבד"
situated_beneficiary.note: No application or transitional clause was found in the consolidated texts or in the quoted amendment; the standalone Sefer HaChukkim text was not retrievable (see deviations). The rule is general in form; coded Yes on the reading that items 1-2 make an enactment Yes when its operative provision has direct legal effect on a pending matter to which only the sitting person is party, the 'motive alone' exclusion applying only where the provision does not itself reach the live matter. On the alternative reading (a rule that successors would also enjoy is never Yes) this cell would be No. The committee chair's statement of 21 March 2023 that the bill bars the High Court and the Attorney General from recusing Netanyahu is a statement of purpose and was not relied on.

situated_beneficiary.person_or_government: The sitting government: Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu as appointing authority, and National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir (an identifiable person in office)
situated_beneficiary.matter: The High Court petition by Tag Meir and other groups, filed in late December 2022, against the Prime Minister's decision to appoint Ben Gvir as National Security Minister, litigated on the reasonableness standard: the Attorney General's filed position of 26 March 2023 was that the appointment is not 'unreasonable in the extreme'; a hearing was held on 3 April 2023; the petition was still pending on 24 July 2023 (its disposition was reported only on 21 February 2024)
situated_beneficiary.admissible_fact: Item 1: a proceeding pending before a court concerning the government's measure (the appointment), on reasonableness grounds, on the day of passage. The operative provision, s.15(d1), bars any court including the High Court of Justice from ruling on the reasonableness of a decision of the government, the Prime Minister or a minister, 'decision' including appointments, and has no clause excluding pending proceedings; it therefore alters the sitting government's legal position in that pending matter, to which no successor is party.
situated_beneficiary.fact_date: Late December 2022 (petition filed); 26 March 2023 (Attorney General's position); 3 April 2023 (hearing); pending through 24 July 2023 (disposition reported 21 February 2024)
situated_beneficiary.source: Times of Israel, 'AG tells High Court she opposes petition to disqualify Ben Gvir as cabinet minister', 28 March 2023; Times of Israel, "'I made mistakes': Ben Gvir tells High Court he's 'refined' since entering politics", 4 April 2023; Times of Israel article reporting the petition's disposition, publication date 21 February 2024 (used for its date and the filing date only); enactment text: s.15(d1) at https://he.wikisource.org/wiki/חוק-יסוד:_השפיטה (Sefer HaChukkim 5783 p. 548); Times of Israel liveblog, 24 July 2023 (64-0 final vote)
situated_beneficiary.support: s.15(d1): "לא ידון בעניין סבירות ההחלטה של הממשלה, של ראש הממשלה או של שר אחר"; data point: 'decision' is defined to include appointments and decisions not to exercise a power.
situated_beneficiary.note: Not relied on: the Yesh Atid and Movement for Quality Government petitions against Justice Minister Levin's refusal to convene the Judicial Selection Committee were filed on 25 July 2023, after passage (Times of Israel, 25 July 2023); the petitions seeking Netanyahu's removal for breach of the conflict-of-interest arrangement (Mivtzar HaDemokratia; MQG) rest on that arrangement rather than on reasonableness; petitions against the amendment itself postdate it. Searches (Times of Israel, and Hebrew searches on ynet, Haaretz, Globes, Calcalist) found no other reasonableness proceeding pending on 24 July 2023. Same interpretive reading as in cell 8; on the alternative reading this cell would be No.

Court outcomes that reached me through search-result titles or search summaries without my opening the pages, all ignored: enactment 6: a Times of Israel headline that the High Court ordered the government to explain the failure to pass the 2020 budget, and a Maariv headline characterizing the court's view of the 'Hauser compromise' as misuse of Knesset authority; enactment 8: Times of Israel, Kipa and Ynet headlines and a search summary that the High Court in January 2024 deferred the recusal law to the next Knesset as 'clearly personal', plus a summary that the court in May 2023 ruled on a contempt petition against Netanyahu; enactment 9: a Times of Israel headline that justices annulled the overhaul law, a Ynet headline and a Hebrew search summary of an 8-7 ruling of 1 January 2024, and a summary that the Ben Gvir appointment petition was rejected and of the January 2023 Deri ruling; enactment 5: a search summary of a September 2017 ruling on the 2017-2018 temporary provision; enactment 4: a JTA 1999 headline and summary that the High Court upheld the 1994 meat-import law; enactment 7: a Times of Israel headline that the court rejected petitions against the nation-state law.

Forbidden-source-derived facts not used: a general web search for the 1969 petition returned Versa (Cardozo) judgment-translation pages for the case on enactment 2 and a search summary derived from them giving the case number, the parties, an order nisi dated 30 April 1969 and a decision date of 3 July 1969. Enactment 9: to establish that the Ben Gvir appointment petition was still pending on 24 July 2023, I opened the Times of Israel article reporting its disposition with an instruction to return only its publication date (21 February 2024) and the petition's filing date; nothing else was returned, but its headline, seen in search results, had already disclosed the disposition.

Enactment 8: the standalone Sefer HaChukkim text of Amendment No. 12 could not be retrieved (Knesset site blocked and not archived; no Wikisource or Nevo page for the amendment). I used an IDI-hosted court filing by the Knesset, dated after passage, solely to extract the quoted text of s.16(b1); grepping the extracted text also exposed lines of the Knesset's own arguments about the amendment's immediate application and summaries of earlier case law on other Basic Laws, which I did not use. No application or transitional clause was found in the quoted amendment or in the consolidated texts.

Sources outside the permitted list consulted: English translations of the 1994 Basic Law at ICL (servat.unibe.ch) and WIPO Lex, used only to locate the provisions before the Hebrew Knesset PDF was obtained; the Hebrew text governs. The 9 February 2023 petition's pendency on 23 March 2023 rests on its filing date, the court's 10 February 2023 response order and the absence of any reported disposition in the permitted press through 24 March 2023; no docket record was reachable.

Not found: the original text of the 1969 financing law (Sefer HaChukkim 550 p. 18), only its amending law of 15 July 1969; a permitted dated source for the 1969 petition or order nisi; the Sefer HaChukkim issue date of the 1969 validation law (S.H. 568); the bill reference of Amendment No. 12 (2023).
